title.en: Fed has 'work to do' if price rises don't ease for Americans, Warsh says
title.zh: 沃什表示，如果美国人的物价上涨没有缓解，美联储还有“工作要做”

summary.en: Kevin Warsh remarks suggest interest rates could be increased if policymakers think inflation is running too high.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The head of the US central bank said policymakers will "have work to do" if they are not confident cost of living pressures are easing for Americans.

Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh said while inflation readings looked better than expected over the summer, they did not show that the current picture had "meaningfully improved".

The new Fed boss stressed that his remarks should not be treated as a guide for future interest rate decisions, but the comments suggest rates could be raised if policymakers believe inflation is too high.

The latest figures showed prices rose 3.4% in the year to July, above the Fed's 2% target.

Warsh made the comments in his first speech at the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium in Wyoming, which sees central bankers, government officials and academics from around the world gather to talk about interest rates, inflation and other economic issues.

Warsh said given prices were rising by more than 2% on annual basis, "the Fed's predominant focus right now should be on prices".

"Here is my standard: We must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do."

The central bank boss has remained tight-lipped about the potential path of interest rates, but investors will have watched his speech closely for any signs of the Fed's approach under his leadership.

The reaction to any decision of US President Donald Trump will be closely watched, with the mid-term elections looming and voters concerned about affordability.

Trump, who appointed Warsh in May, repeatedly criticised and pushed his predecessor Jerome Powell to cut interest rates. The president has previously said rate hikes "just keeps the country down".

Warsh issued a plea in his speech to not label his remark as "forward guidance" and said he believed the practice of sending signals to the markets on future interest rate decisions, adopted in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis, had "overstayed its welcome".

"Oversharing policy deliberations and overcommitting to future decisions can lead markets, businesses, and households astray," he said, adding it also inhibited the Fed the "freedom to make the right calls when it's time to decide".

Interest rates were left unchanged between 3.5% and 3.75% in July for the fifth time in a row amid concerns over inflation due to the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran, which has caused as surge in global oil prices.

Following Warsh's remarks, the rates market showed growing expectations of an interest rate rise in September, according to CME data.

Analysts at Capital Economics said Warsh's speech delivered a "far clearer - and hawkish - message" and that it left "the door open to a hike" earlier than previously...
body.zh: 美联储行长表示，如果政策制定者对美国人的生活成本压力是否有所缓解没有信心，他们将“有工作要做”。 美联储主席凯文·沃什表示，虽然夏季通胀数据看起来好于预期，但并未表明当前情况“显着改善”。 这位新任美联储主席强调，他的言论不应被视为未来利率决策的指南，但该言论表明，如果政策制定者认为通胀过高，可能会加息。 最新数据显示，截至 7 月份的一年内，物价上涨了 3.4%，高于美联储 2% 的目标。 沃什在怀俄明州杰克逊霍尔年度经济政策研讨会上的首次演讲中发表了上述言论，来自世界各地的央行行长、政府官员和学者齐聚一堂，讨论利率、通胀和其他经济问题。 Warsh表示，鉴于物价年增长率超过2%，“美联储目前的主要关注点应该是物价”。 “我的标准是：我们必须相信潜在的通胀正在以足够的速度明确地实现我们的目标。否则，我们还有工作要做。” 这位央行行长对潜在的利率走势仍然守口如瓶，但投资者将密切关注他的讲话，寻找美联储在他领导下采取行动的任何迹象。 随着中期选举的临近以及选民对负担能力的担忧，人们对美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的任何决定的反应都将受到密切关注。 特朗普于5月任命沃什为总统，多次批评并敦促其前任杰罗姆·鲍威尔降息。总统此前曾表示，加息“只会让国家陷入低迷”。 沃什在演讲中请求不要将自己的言论贴上“前瞻性指引”的标签，并表示他认为2008年金融危机后就未来利率决策向市场发出信号的做法“已经过时了”。 他表示：“过度分享政策审议和过度致力于未来决策可能会导致市场、企业和家庭误入歧途。”他补充说，这也限制了美联储“在需要做出决定时做出正确决定的自由”。 由于美国和伊朗之间持续的冲突导致全球油价飙升，人们担心通货膨胀，7月份利率连续第五次维持在3.5%至3.75%之间。 根据芝商所数据，在沃什发表讲话后，利率市场对 9 月份加息的预期日益增强。 凯投宏观的分析师表示，沃什的讲话传达了“更加清晰、更加鹰派的信息”，并且比之前更早地“为加息敞开了大门”。

title.en: Uganda: World's 'youngest monarch' dies aged 34
title.zh: 乌干达：世界上“最年轻的君主”去世，享年34岁

summary.en: Oyo Nyimba, once recognized as the world's youngest reigning monarch, has died in his mid-30s. As one of Uganda's traditional monarchs, he took the throne of the Tooro kingdom in 1995, aged just 3.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 奥约·宁巴（Oyo Nyimba）曾被认为是世界上最年轻的在位君主，现已去世，年仅 30 多岁。作为乌干达传统君主之一，他于1995年登上托罗王国王位，年仅3岁。 托罗总理周四晚间宣布，乌干达前殖民传统王国托罗的国王奥约·宁巴 (Oyo Nyimba) 去世，年仅 34 岁。 托罗地区领导人卡尔文·阿姆斯特朗·卢米埃尔·阿基基 (Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki) 在社交媒体上表示：“我怀着深切的悲伤和沉重的心情宣布托罗的奥穆卡马国王奥约·宁巴·卡班巴·卡班巴·伊古鲁·鲁基迪四世去世。” 乌干达是一个共和国，由议会和名义上选举产生的国家元首、长期任职的总统约韦里·穆塞韦尼（Yoweri Museveni）统治，他自 1986 年以来一直执政。 但该国保留了几个传统的君主制，这些君主制仍然按照前殖民时期的方式统治着它们的王国。他们的权力在很大程度上是象征性的，但他们具有相当大的文化和社会影响力。 尽管 1962 年脱离英国殖民统治独立后，一位共和党总统表示他希望统一这个新生国家，从而禁止了传统君主制，但穆塞韦尼还是在 1993 年恢复了传统君主制。 奥约·宁巴 (Oyo Nyimba) 可以说是其中最知名的一个，尤其是因为他不寻常的故事，他于 1995 年年仅 3 岁就登上了王位。 地区领导人阿基基 (Akiiki) 表示，国王于周四晚些时候去世，但没有透露死因。他表示，稍后将发表一份包含葬礼和哀悼安排等更多细节的官方声明。 他呼吁托罗人民“在这个困难时期保持团结、冷静和祈祷”。 阿基基还对这位未婚的年轻国王发表了一项令人惊讶的说法，他从很小的时候起就被视为乌干达最有资格的单身汉。 “王室的连续性是有保证的，”他说。 “陛下留下一位王子作为继承人，他的身份将在适当的时候按照托罗王国的传统和习俗正式公布。” 奥约·宁巴（Oyo Nyimba）的去世引发了网上的悲痛和乌干达全国的广泛报道。 奥约出生于1992年4月16日，是已故奥姆卡马·帕特里克·大卫·马修·卡沃约·奥利米三世和王后贝斯特·凯米吉萨·卡博约​​的第二个孩子，有两个姐妹。 1995年，他父亲去世后，他在乌干达西部靠近刚果边境的托罗地区登上了王位。 他作为现代“男孩国王”的不同寻常的地位在他统治初期引起了相当大的兴趣，包括多次访问托罗的前利比亚强人穆阿迈尔·卡扎菲等世界领导人。 奥约的母亲是他年轻时的重要顾问之一，总统约韦里也是如此……

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 我们对尼泊尔和西藏致命洪水的了解

summary.en: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Devastating landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead and thousands more missing.

At least 579 people have been killed and nearly 2,000 people remain unaccounted for, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

On Wednesday, flood water tore through the border region, sweeping away homes and roads, local officials have said.

Rescue workers say they now face a critical moment to reach remaining survivors as fears mount of further flooding in the disaster's aftermath.

Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating floods early on Wednesday.

However, the US Geological Survey (USGS) later confirmed that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse" - when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to the agency, causing "subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream".

Powerful flood water and debris travelled some 62 miles (100km) downstream from the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi Rivers, the USGS said, sweeping through towns popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims in northern Nepal.

Footage showed a wall of mud and rock sweeping away buildings, roads and vehicles as people fled in the Nuwakot region.

In one video, a towering wall of water and mud was seen rushing down a gorge along the Trishuli River and enveloping the Rasuwagadhi Border checkpoint, a multi-storey building on the Nepalese side.

Gyirong Port, over the border, was also hit. A number of deaths were reported in Tibetan villages.

Scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events as rescue efforts continue. Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

"I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, [which] dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIDMOD) has warned secondary flooding could occur in the coming days as a result of debris that washed into the river systems.

The ICIDMOD said it was assessing whether the Trishuli River had been temporarily blocked in narrow sections. If this is the case, it is at risk of forming a landslide dam and a second flood.

Separately, China has warned there was a "high risk" a lake that formed after the landslide may burst its banks, causing fresh flooding downstream. As of Friday, an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of water had...
body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生的毁灭性山体滑坡和山洪造成大范围破坏，造成数百人死亡、数千人失踪。 据尼泊尔国家减少灾害风险和管理局称，至少 579 人死亡，近 2,000 人下落不明。 当地官员表示，周三，洪水席卷了边境地区，冲毁了房屋和道路。 救援人员表示，他们现在面临着救助剩余幸存者的关键时刻，因为人们越来越担心灾难发生后会发生进一步的洪水。 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生地震的初步报道让许多人相信地震导致了山体滑坡，进而导致了周三早些时候的毁灭性洪水。 然而，美国地质调查局（USGS）后来证实，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 据该机构称，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级，“随后对下游造成了灾难性影响”。 美国地质勘探局表示，强大的洪水和碎片从特里苏里河和博特科希河向下游流动约62英里（100公里），席卷了尼泊尔北部深受登山游客和朝圣者欢迎的城镇。 视频显示，努瓦科特地区的人们纷纷逃离，泥石墙冲走了建筑物、道路和车辆。 在一段视频中，人们看到一堵高耸的水和泥墙沿着特里苏里河冲下峡谷，包围了拉苏瓦加迪边境检查站，这是尼泊尔一侧的一座多层建筑。 边境另一边的吉隆口岸也受到袭击。据报道，西藏村庄已有多人死亡。 随着救援工作的继续，科学家们正试图拼凑出事件的确切顺序。牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，在洪水袭击尼泊尔和西藏之前“几小时或几天”，冰川可能已经崩塌。 他告诉英国广播公司：“我认为，巨大的碎片浪潮表明，首先发生了山体滑坡，水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后引发了一场巨大的洪水。” 国际山地综合开发中心（ICIDMOD）警告称，由于碎片冲入河流系统，未来几天可能会发生二次洪水。 ICIDMOD 表示正在评估 Trishuli 河的狭窄河段是否被暂时堵塞。如果真是这样，就有形成滑坡坝和二次洪水的危险。 另外，中国警告说，山体滑坡后形成的湖泊存在“高风险”，可能会决堤，导致下游出现新的洪水。截至周五，估计有 250 万立方米的水...

title.en: BBC tracks one week of Israeli settler violence in occupied West Bank
title.zh: BBC 追踪以色列定居者在被占领的约旦河西岸一周的暴力事件

summary.en: The BBC's Lucy Williamson reports on settler attacks on Palestinians, which have been observed over the last week alone.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Violence by Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank is set to reach record levels this year, as human rights groups warn that they are increasingly spreading into new areas of the territory.

Attacks on Palestinians have risen under Israel's current government, alongside a rapid increase in Israeli settlements, illegal under international law.

The BBC's Lucy Williamson has been tracking settler attacks on Palestinians, which have been observed over the last week alone.
body.zh: 被占领的约旦河西岸犹太定居者的暴力行为今年将达到创纪录水平，人权组织警告称，这些暴力行为正日益蔓延到该领土的新地区。 在以色列现任政府领导下，针对巴勒斯坦人的袭击有所增加，以色列定居点也迅速增加，根据国际法，这是非法的。 BBC 的露西·威廉姆森一直在追踪定居者对巴勒斯坦人的袭击，仅在上周就观察到了这种情况。

title.en: Africa's aging autocrats fight to stay in power
title.zh: 非洲年迈的独裁者们为保住权力而战

summary.en: Some of Africa's longest-serving leaders are employing various tactics to extend their rule as they age, facing new challenges from succession battles and public pressure.
summary.zh: 随着年龄增长，非洲一些在位时间最长的领导人正采取不同策略以延长其统治，但年龄、继位之争和公众压力带来了新的挑战。

body.en:
As some of Africa's longest-serving leaders grow older, they are using different tactics to extend their rule. But age, succession battles and public pressure pose new challenges.

Power can be seductive, and many who possess it want to hold on to it for as long as possible. The leaders of China  and Russia , for example, cleared the way for additional terms years ago, and in the United States, the president occasionally speaks of another run for office, even though the Constitution does not allow it.

From the perspective of Paul Biya, however, Chinese President  Xi Jinping , Russian President  Vladimir Putin and US President  Donald Trump are still relatively new to office.

Cameroon's president has been head of state since 1982. In 2025, he began his eighth term , which is officially due to end on November 6, 2032, just a few months before his 100th birthday.

The 93-year-old has given no official indication that he intends to step down , and the position of vice president remains vacant. As a result, Biya is one of several African leaders who have taken further steps this year to secure their grip on power .

During his 44 years in office, Biya has built a stable network of loyal allies that keeps the machinery of government running despite his lengthy absences.

The 93-year-old has now spent two and a half months in Geneva, Switzerland, continuing to issue decrees and make personnel decisions from abroad. In mid-June, his spokesperson denied rumors that Biya was receiving treatment in a hospital and stated that he was in good health.

"There is continuity, but that also means there is little momentum for reform within the government,” Beverly Ochieng, senior analyst at consultancy Global Risk, told DW.

And while Biya's power apparatus has helped cushion the impact of the president's long absence, that does not necessarily mean the most influential figures on the ground are united. After all, a post-Biya era is now in sight , and several of his allies are rumored to have ambitions of succeeding him.

"When everyone is lining up to potentially succeed Biya, it also means that the elites may begin challenging one another," Ochieng said. Such rivalry, she warned, could lead to major disruptions, including the possibility of a military coup.

Analyst Levi Mboushou recently voiced similar concerns on DW's Africalink podcast.

"Everyone feels the fear and uncertainty, but no one dares to look directly at it because we all have to deal with this repressive regime. You see something, but you say nothing. That is the situation in Cameroon  at the moment."

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni is only slightly younger, both in age and years in office.

The 81-year-old has been president since 1986 and, like Biya, recently...
body.zh: 随着非洲一些任职时间最长的领导人年龄的增长，他们正在使用不同的策略来延长他们的统治。但年龄、继承之争和公众压力带来了新的挑战。 权力是诱人的，许多拥有权力的人都想尽可能长时间地保留权力。例如，中国和俄罗斯领导人多年前就为追加任期扫清了道路，而在美国，总统偶尔会谈到再次竞选总统，尽管宪法不允许。 然而，从保罗·比亚的角度来看，中国国家主席习近平、俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普仍相对较新上任。 喀麦隆总统自 1982 年起担任国家元首。2025 年，他开始了第八个任期，正式任期将于 2032 年 11 月 6 日结束，距他的 100 岁生日仅几个月。 这位93岁的老人没有正式表示他打算辞职，副总统职位仍然空缺。因此，比亚是今年采取进一步措施以确保掌权的几位非洲领导人之一。 在其 44 年的执政生涯中，比亚建立了一个稳定的忠诚盟友网络，尽管他长期缺席，但该网络仍使政府机构保持运转。 这位93岁的老人如今已经在瑞士日内瓦度过了两个半月的时间，继续在国外发布法令、做出人事决定。 6月中旬，其发言人否认了比亚正在医院接受治疗的传闻，并表示比亚身体状况良好。 咨询公司Global Risk的高级分析师贝弗利·奥钦(Beverly Ochieng)对德国之声表示：“存在连续性，但这也意味着政府内部改革动力不大。” 尽管比亚的权力机构帮助缓解了总统长期缺席的影响，但这并不一定意味着当地最有影响力的人物是团结的。毕竟，后比亚时代即将到来，据传他的几个盟友都有接替他的野心。 奥钦说：“当每个人都在排队等待比亚的接班人时，这也意味着精英们可能会开始相互挑战。”她警告说，这种竞争可能会导致重大混乱，包括发生军事政变的可能性。 分析师 Levi Mboushou 最近在德国之声的 Africalink 播客上表达了类似的担忧。 “每个人都感受到恐惧和不确定性，但没有人敢直视它，因为我们都必须应对这个高压政权。你看到了一些东西，但你什么也没说。这就是喀麦隆目前的情况。” 乌干达总统约韦里·穆塞韦尼无论是在年龄还是在任年限上都只稍微年轻一些。 这位 81 岁的老人自 1986 年以来一直担任总统，和比亚一样，最近......

title.en: Oslo mayor calls off wedding ceremony after death of Norway's king
title.zh: 挪威国王去世后奥斯陆市长取消婚礼

summary.en: Anne Lindboe, the mayor of Norway's capital, had planned to marry her fiance on Friday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Oslo's Mayor Anne Lindboe has called off her wedding ceremony because of the death of King Harald V of Norway.

The wedding with her fiancé Pål Sandvid was planned to take place on Friday but was postponed after the king died earlier the same day, her political adviser confirmed to the BBC.

"It's hard to imagine an Oslo and a Norway without you. You didn't need a crowd to be king," Lindboe wrote in a tribute to the late monarch on Instagram.

Harald reigned for 35 years and died at the national hospital in Norway's capital, where he was being treated for a rare blood condition. His son, King Haakon VIII , ascended the throne on Friday.

"Even the majority of Norwegians who never met you in person still felt like they knew you," Lindboe added in her tribute.

After five years together, Lindboe announced the couple's engagement in June this year.

The late king was a popular and reforming leader in Norway who modernised the monarchy.

He broke with tradition by marrying a commoner, Queen Sonja, and served as a unifying figure during Norway's most difficult moments.

Members of the public have been gathering to lay flowers at a memorial outside the Royal Palace in Oslo.

Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said in a televised memorial address that his country was "united in grief and gratitude" for Harald's service and that his "legacy lives on".

The UK's King Charles III said he was mourning his "dear cousin". King Harald V was a second cousin of the King's mother, Queen Elizabeth II.
body.zh: 由于挪威国王哈拉尔五世去世，奥斯陆市长安妮·林德博取消了她的婚礼。 她的政治顾问向英国广播公司证实，她与未婚夫帕尔·桑维德的婚礼原定于周五举行，但由于国王当天早些时候去世，婚礼被推迟。 “很难想象没有你的奥斯陆和挪威。你不需要人群就能成为国王，”林德博在 Instagram 上向已故君主致敬时写道。 哈拉尔统治了 35 年，最终在挪威首都国家医院去世，当时他正在医院接受罕见的血液病治疗。他的儿子哈康八世国王于周五登上王位。 “即使是大多数从未见过你本人的挪威人仍然感觉他们认识你，”林德博在致敬中补充道。 在一起五年后，林德博于今年六月宣布两人订婚。 这位已故国王是挪威一位受欢迎的改革领袖，他实现了君主制的现代化。 他打破传统，与平民索尼娅王后结婚，并在挪威最困难的时刻发挥了团结作用。 公众聚集在奥斯陆皇宫外的纪念碑前献花。 挪威首相乔纳斯·加尔·斯托尔在电视转播的追悼会上表示，挪威对哈拉尔的服务“深感悲痛和感激”，并表示他的“遗产将继续存在”。 英国国王查理三世表示，他正在哀悼他的“亲爱的表弟”。哈拉尔五世国王是国王母亲伊丽莎白二世女王的远房表弟。

title.en: Shootings surge as drug gangs torment Brussels
title.zh: 贩毒团伙折磨布鲁塞尔枪击案激增

summary.en: This year alone there have been more than 65 shootings in the Belgian capital, as drug crime soars.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Last Monday night, drug gangs turned Salvatore's pizzeria in Brussels into a crime scene.

"We dropped to the floor. I had clients eating on the terrace with children. Look, we can see the bullet impacts everywhere."

His restaurant sits on a pretty little square in St Gilles. It's a central area of the city, close to the international Midi train station, where passengers arrive on trains from London and Paris.

Shootings related to drug trafficking have become routine in the Belgian capital over the past couple of years. There were over 100 in 2025 alone, and more than 65 shootings so far this year.

Now Murielle and her dog Chéva are sitting at that exact spot, just across the street: "We can still see the trace of the pool of blood."

"I like it here. It's like a little village inside the city. Even the drug dealers used to be polite and decent. I would just tell them to go further away and they'd say, 'Yes, ok mama!'"

Drug dealing is happening in plain sight here. Only five minutes after I arrive, I witness a transaction.

A buyer walks up to the seller, shakes their hand, and walks away with the drugs. Crack has become widely consumed amongst the poorest in this area of Brussels.

"Things have changed in the past six months," says Murielle. "The business has intensified. Sometimes you even see consumers queuing to buy drugs. And now gangs are fighting over this spot."

A successful drug-dealing point in Brussels nets up to €50,000 ($58,000; £43,000) per day or more for the dealer, according to the chief of Brussels South Police, Jurgen de Landsheer.

Organised crime in the Belgian capital has become significantly more violent, he says.

At the heart of it all is money. There are more than 200 drug-dealing points across the city, according to the police.

The rise of drug-related violence in the Belgian capital echoes the situation of other European cities such as the French port of Marseille.

Cocaine has become widely available in Europe, the continent's ports serving as entry points for the drug. The port of Antwerp, just 40km (25 miles) away, has seen record cocaine seizures in recent years.

Jurgen de Landsheer says gangs in Brussels are now adopting methods seen in Marseille, although he insists his city has not reached the same level of violence.

"We don't have no-go zones here in Brussels. It's not easy to go in some neighbourhoods, but we go everywhere. We don't want to become like some neighbourhoods in Marseille, so we'll do everything to stop it."

body.zh: 上周一晚上，贩毒团伙将布鲁塞尔的萨尔瓦多披萨店变成了犯罪现场。 “我们倒在地板上。我的客户带着孩子在露台上吃饭。看，我们到处都可以看到子弹的撞击。” 他的餐厅坐落在圣吉尔的一个漂亮的小广场上。它位于城市的中心区域，靠近国际 Midi 火车站，乘客从伦敦和巴黎乘坐火车抵达这里。 过去几年来，与贩毒有关的枪击事件在比利时首都已成为家常便饭。仅 2025 年一年就发生了 100 多起枪击事件，今年迄今已发生超过 65 起枪击事件。 现在，穆里埃尔和她的狗切瓦正坐在街对面的那个地方：“我们仍然可以看到血泊的痕迹。” “我喜欢这里。它就像城里的一个小村庄。即使是毒贩也曾经很有礼貌和正派。我只是告诉他们走远一点，他们会说，‘是的，好的，妈妈！’” 毒品交易在这里随处可见。我到达后仅五分钟，就见证了一笔交易。 一名买家走到卖家面前，与他们握手，然后带着毒品走开。快克已成为布鲁塞尔这一地区最贫困人群的广泛消费。 “过去六个月情况发生了变化，”穆里埃尔说。 “生意愈演愈烈，有时甚至看到消费者排队购买毒品。现在黑帮正在争夺这个位置。” 布鲁塞尔南部警察局局长尤尔根·德·兰谢尔 (Jurgen de Landsheer) 表示，布鲁塞尔一个成功的毒品交易点每天为毒贩赚取的利润高达 50,000 欧元（58,000 美元；43,000 英镑）或更多。 他说，比利时首都的有组织犯罪变得更加暴力。 这一切的核心是金钱。据警方称，全市有200多个贩毒点。 比利时首都毒品相关暴力事件的兴起与法国马赛港等其他欧洲城市的情况相呼应。 可卡因在欧洲已变得很普遍，该大陆的港口是该毒品的入境点。距离酒店仅 40 公里（25 英里）的安特卫普港近年来缉获的可卡因数量创历史新高。 于尔根·德·兰谢尔表示，布鲁塞尔的帮派现在正在采用马赛的方法，尽管他坚称他的城市尚未达到同样的暴力程度。 “我们在布鲁塞尔没有禁区。有些街区不太容易进入，但我们可以去任何地方。我们不想变得像马赛的一些街区一样，所以我们会尽一切努力阻止这种情况。” 闭路电视录像显示，两名骑着摩托车的男子停在大楼前，用一把看起来像 AK-47 的东西朝门口开了几枪，然后骑着摩托车离开。 这标志着事态升级，因为这是犯罪分子首次针对警察。通常情况下，枪击事件...

title.en: Serbia: Keeping EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
title.zh: 塞尔维亚：在关键选举前让欧盟和俄罗斯参与其中

summary.en: As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.

Smoke from the wildfires still hangs over parts of Serbia , but as the flames slowly recede, another debate is taking shape in their wake — one that has less to do with firefighting and more with politics.

In early August, wildfires swept across Serbia, affecting more than 3,500 hectares (8,600 acres) in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve alone. For days, firefighters, soldiers and helicopters battled the flames.

Then a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in the southern city of Nis. Serbia had turned to Moscow for help, making Russia the first foreign country it asked to provide a firefighting aircraft. Pro-government media greeted its arrival with celebratory coverage, dubbing the aircraft the "Russian beast."

"Considering that there are no firefighting aircraft of this capacity available within the European Union , the arriving Russian aircraft will significantly strengthen our capacities to fight the fires," said Luka Causic, head of the Serbian Interior Ministry's Department for Emergency Situations.

The episode, however, was already being viewed through a geopolitical lens, as Serbia had sought Russian assistance before activating the EU's emergency mechanism.

When it did, the response was swift. Brussels mobilized four helicopters from its strategic rescEU reserve , based in Czechia, Romania and Slovakia, along with ground firefighting teams from Germany and Romania.

Vucic rejected the idea that turning to Russia first was a foreign-policy decision or a sign of Serbia's political alignment with Moscow.

"As far as equipment and resources are concerned, we are a European giant. The helicopters we received from Europe to fight the fires are less capable than ours and have a lower carrying capacity than our own," Vucic said during a visit to the Deliblato Sands.

The wildfire episode came less than two weeks after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made his first official visit to Serbia.

The two presidents reaffirmed their support for each other's territorial integrity, which is particularly significant for Belgrade because Ukraine does not recognise Kosovo's independence.

But Vucic is also trying to keep the other side on board, says Vuk Vuksanovic , a political scientist and foreign-policy lecturer at King's College London.

Vuksanovic argues that Vucic's engagement with Zelenskyy must therefore be portrayed in Moscow not as a fundamental shift in Serbia's relationship with Russia, but as a response to Western pressure and Serbia's own interests.

body.zh: 随着塞尔维亚大选走向不确定，总统亚历山大·武契奇正在平衡与俄罗斯和欧盟野心的关系。但日益加剧的地缘政治紧张局势和国内压力正在缩小他的回旋余地。 野火产生的烟雾仍然笼罩在塞尔维亚部分地区，但随着火焰慢慢消退，另一场辩论正在形成——这场辩论与消防无关，更多与政治有关。 8 月初，野火席卷了塞尔维亚，仅德利布拉托金沙特别自然保护区就影响了超过 3,500 公顷（8,600 英亩）的土地。连日来，消防员、士兵和直升机一直在与大火搏斗。 随后一架俄罗斯伊尔76型消防机抵达南部城市尼什。塞尔维亚向莫斯科寻求帮助，使俄罗斯成为第一个请求提供消防飞机的国家。亲政府媒体以庆祝性报道欢迎这架飞机的到来，称这架飞机为“俄罗斯野兽”。 塞尔维亚内政部紧急情况司司长卢卡·考西克表示：“考虑到欧盟境内没有具备这种能力的消防飞机，抵达的俄罗斯飞机将大大增强我们的灭火能力。” 然而，这一事件已经被从地缘政治的角度看待，因为塞尔维亚在启动欧盟紧急机制之前曾寻求俄罗斯的援助。 当它发生时，反应很快。布鲁塞尔从其驻捷克、罗马尼亚和斯洛伐克的战略救援储备中调动了四架直升机，以及来自德国和罗马尼亚的地面消防队。 武契奇否认首先转向俄罗斯是一项外交政策决定或塞尔维亚与莫斯科政治结盟的标志。 “就设备和资源而言，我们是欧洲巨头。我们从欧洲接收的用于灭火的直升机的能力不如我们的，运载能力也低于我们自己的，”武契奇在参观德利布拉托金沙时说道。 这场山火发生在乌克兰总统泽连斯基首次正式访问塞尔维亚后不到两周。 两国总统重申支持彼此的领土完整，这对贝尔格莱德尤为重要，因为乌克兰不承认科索沃独立。 但伦敦国王学院政治学家兼外交政策讲师武克·武克萨诺维奇 (Vuk Vuksanovic) 表示，武契奇也在努力让对方参与其中。 武克萨诺维奇认为，因此莫斯科必须将武契奇与泽连斯基的接触描述为塞尔维亚与俄罗斯关系的根本转变，而不是对西方压力和塞尔维亚自身利益的回应。 “武契奇现在...

title.en: South Korea leans toward military conscription for women
title.zh: 韩国倾向于女性入伍

summary.en: Facing a population decline, fewer potential service members and calls for social equality to be extended to national military service, Korea is inching closer to breaking the taboo on women on the front line.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Facing a population decline, fewer potential service members and calls for social equality to be extended to national military service, Korea is inching closer to breaking the taboo on women on the front line.

Nearly 60% of South Koreans are now in favor of young women serving mandatory military service alongside their male counterparts, according to a recent survey, representing a significant shift in the long-held taboo against women being obliged to defend the nation.

Thousands of women already serve in the South Korean armed forces on a voluntary basis, but the debate over mandatory service has always been delicate.

Now, for a series of reasons that include a falling birth rate and shrinking number of recruits as well as an insistence that social equality means that women should also serve, the issue has re-emerged ahead of a reform of the national defense plan scheduled to be released this autumn.

Yet, there are still those who insist women should be kept away from the front lines and, instead, that South Korea should invest more in drones and other advanced technologies.

"South Korea's male-centered conscription system has long been closely connected to traditional gender roles," said Hyobin Lee, a professor at Sogang University in Seoul.

"Men were generally expected to protect the country and the family and to fight in wartime, while women were expected to take primary responsibility for childbirth, childcare and the household," she told DW.

A second factor is the intensifying debate about gender equality , a debate in large part driven by young men, she said.

"South Korean men generally perform their military service in their early 20s, which interrupts their education, employment or early career development," Lee said.

"At the same time, gender equality has become an increasingly important social value, and women's opportunities in education and employment have expanded."

"As a result, some younger men ask a very simple question: If society expects equality in rights and opportunities, why does one of the country's most significant civic obligations — military service — still fall only on men?"

Another contributing factor is the change in the nature of the military itself, with a shift away from physically demanding combat roles that were perceived as being more suited to men and the emergence of a national defense more heavily reliant on technology.

This includes unmanned systems, cyber capabilities, information and communications technology and others that do not require physical strength.

body.zh: 面对人口下降、潜在服役人员减少以及将社会平等延伸至国家兵役的呼声，韩国正一步步打破女性在前线的禁忌。 最近的一项调查显示，近 60% 的韩国人现在支持年轻女性与男性同行一起服义务兵役，这标志着长期以来反对女性有义务保卫国家的禁忌发生了重大转变。 已有数千名女性自愿在韩国武装部队服役，但关于强制服役的争论一直很微妙。 现在，由于出生率下降、入伍人数减少以及坚持社会平等意味着妇女也应该服役等一系列原因，这个问题在定于今年秋天发布的国防计划改革之前重新出现。 然而，仍然有人坚持认为女性应该远离前线，相反，韩国应该在无人机和其他先进技术上进行更多投资。 首尔西江大学教授李孝彬 (Hyobin Lee) 表示：“韩国以男性为中心的征兵制度长期以来与传统性别角色密切相关。” 她告诉德国之声：“人们普遍期望男性保护国家和家庭，并在战时参战，而女性则被期望承担生育、照顾孩子和家庭的主要责任。” 她说，第二个因素是关于性别平等的争论日益激烈，这场争论在很大程度上是由年轻男性推动的。 “韩国男性通常在 20 岁出头服兵役，这会中断他们的教育、就业或早期职业发展，”Lee 说。 “与此同时，性别平等已成为越来越重要的社会价值，女性受教育和就业的机会不断扩大。” “因此，一些年轻人提出了一个非常简单的问题：如果社会期望权利和机会平等，为什么这个国家最重要的公民义务之一——服兵役——仍然只落在男性身上？” 另一个影响因素是军队本身性质的变化，人们认为更适合男性的体力要求较高的战斗角色的转变，以及国防更加依赖技术的出现。 这包括无人系统、网络能力、信息和通信技术以及其他不需要体力的系统。 根据保守倾向改革党的政策研究机构改革研究所于 8 月 20 日发布的这项研究，近 60% 的受访者赞成……

title.en: Australian woman feared missing in Nepal flood makes contact as disaster worsens
title.zh: 澳大利亚妇女担心在尼泊尔洪水中失踪，随着灾难的恶化，她与人取得了联系

summary.en: An Australian woman caught up in deadly flooding in Nepal has made contact with family.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australian authorities are urgently trying to reach a woman who made contact with family after surviving catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) is engaging with local authorities on plans to assist the woman, who is understood to have been last reported in a remote area several days' hike from Kathmandu.

At least 38 Australians remain missing after an ice avalanche on Wednesday triggered Nepal's worst natural disaster in more than a decade.

Heavy continued rainfall is making rescue conditions difficult and unpredictable.

Further severe flooding, landslides and debris flows are predicted in the affected areas of Nepal and Tibet while a lake formed by the landslide has started to overflow.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

At least 538 people have died, Nepalese authorities said, while almost 1,000 remain missing.

Australian woman Sumi Adhikari was on a pilgrimage on the China-Nepal border when the catastrophic flash flooding hit.

Her husband Kailash Mansowar, who has not heard from her since, has travelled to the region from Sydney to find her, guided only by her iPhone's last location.

"I am here in Nepal now (since) yesterday and working with local authorities to find further information," he told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) on Friday.

Like many missing Australians, Adhikari was undertaking a group tour, in her case with the Isha Foundation.

She left Kathmandu on 14 August after flying from Sydney to trek to a sacred site near Tibet's Mount Kailash.

"Even the smallest piece of information could help bring her home," a widely shared post on social media announcing her disappearance reads.

A separate group of 15 Australians, including two boys aged 11 and 14, were travelling with US-based tourism operator Himalayan Glacier Adventure and Travel Company.

Sydney doctor Manoj Dharmaratnam, who was invited to join the sacred pilgrimage but chose not to go, prescribed several of his friends altitude medication and conducted injury assessments before they left Australia.

"One of them had an injury and I did tell her, maybe you're not fit to go on this trek," Dr Dharmaratnam told AAP.

"She actually called up and cancelled her trip ... but then she said I've bought the ticket, so I might as well go."

The Himalayan Glacier group included a well-respected Sydney couple with two sons in their 20s, both studying medicine in NSW, he said.

At least four Australians were travelling separately to tour groups, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said on Friday.

body.en:
Norway's King Harald, a reformer who emerged from the shadow of his well-loved, extrovert father and spent more than three decades on the throne, died on Friday at the age of 89, the royal palace said, at a time of multiple crises for the Norwegian royal family.

"King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday 28 August," the royal palace said on its website.

Harald, who was Europe's oldest living monarch, was taken to hospital on 17 August. The palace said doctors were treating him for a bacterial infection in his blood.

In 2024, he had been hospitalised for an infection while on holiday in Malaysia and received a temporary pacemaker at a hospital there. The Norwegian armed forces flew him back home, and he was later fitted with a permanent device.

That same year, Harald, Norway's ceremonial head of state since 1991, said he would reduce the number of official engagements he took part in but ruled out abdication, insisting that his oath as king was for life.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Crown Princess Mette-Marit, married to Harald's son Crown Prince Haakon, is facing intense scrutiny for her friendship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, a relationship for which she has apologised.

Her son Marius Hoiby, born from a relationship predating her marriage to Haakon, was found guilty in June of two out of four counts of rape and one count of domestic violence and sentenced to four years in prison after a seven-week trial. Both he and the prosecution have appealed the sentence.

Two days after Marius was convicted, the palace said Mette-Marit had undergone a successful lung transplant, without specifying when the procedure took place.

After several weeks of recovery in hospital, she returned home and celebrated her silver wedding anniversary with Haakon in August.

Support for the monarchy dropped to 60 per cent in February 2026, from 70 per cent the previous month, according to a Norstat poll published by state broadcaster NRK, rising slightly to 64 per cent in May.

Harald has remained consistently popular with Norwegians. According to the February poll, he was the royal who best represented the Norwegian royal family, with a score of 9.2, on a scale of one to 10.

A great-great-grandchild of Britain's Queen Victoria, Harald acceded to the throne in 1991 and gradually introduced modern touches that brought a ceremonial post, seen mainly as a symbol of national independence, into the 21st century.

The popular king played a crucial role in comforting the nation in times of mourning.

When far-right, anti-Islam convicted terrorist Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 people in 2011 in Oslo and on Utøya...

summary.en: A joint appeal has been launched by Australian charities to support communities devastated by flooding and landslides along the Nepal-China border.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Entire communities have been devastated by severe flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, with homes, roads, bridges and critical infrastructure destroyed.

Search and rescue operations remain underway, while thousands of people are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean drinking water and medical assistance.

In response, 14 Australian charities have joined forces to launch a national appeal.

The Emergency Action Alliance (EAA) has launched the Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal, bringing together a variety of charities to support communities affected by the disaster.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The alliance says donations will help provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, hygiene supplies and medical care.

Access to some affected communities remains difficult, with damaged roads and ongoing weather conditions hampering efforts to reach people in need.

Australians are encouraged to donate through the EAA website or by calling 1300 939 000.

The charities participating in the appeal are Save the Children Australia, Plan International Australia, Oxfam Australia, Australia for UNHCR, ActionAid Australia, CARE Australia, Caritas Australia, ADRA, Act for Peace, Anglican Overseas Aid, Australian Lutheran World Service, Baptist World Aid Australia, CBM Australia and Tearfund Australia.

EAA executive director Kerren Morris said the appeal provided Australians with a trusted way to support people affected by the disaster.

"Emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water and medical support are urgently needed now, while longer-term recovery efforts will continue for many months," she said in a statement.

The charities involved bring different areas of humanitarian expertise to the response, with organisations and their local partners working to provide immediate assistance to affected communities.

Save the Children is focusing on supporting children and families affected by humanitarian emergencies.

Oxfam Australia's humanitarian work includes support for essential services such as clean water, sanitation and emergency assistance.

Australia for UNHCR is the UN refugee agency's national partner in Australia, and is supporting humanitarian assistance through the UNHCR network.

The charities involved are continuing to assess the scale of the disaster and humanitarian needs in affected communities.

The EAA says its members are working to determine where support is most urgently needed as search and rescue operations continue.

The appeal has been endorsed by the Australian Council for International Development (ACFID), the peak body for Australian non-government organisations...

title.en: The threat hanging over Nepal: What happens next after the deadly floods?
title.zh: 尼泊尔面临的威胁：致命洪水过后接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Another disaster could strike Nepal as rescuers search for survivors and communities face a long road to recovery.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 1,400 people remain missing after a catastrophic flash flood swept through communities along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing at least 472 people across Nepal and Tibet.

Thirty-nine Australians are among those reported missing as rescue efforts continue.

And the danger is not over, experts warn, with another disaster still possible in Nepal despite the difficulty of predicting when, where or how severe it could be.

"This can be the next day, after a couple of days or can be months later, but it is less likely that we will have this scale of flood again," Monash University glacier researcher Levan Tielidze said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Scientists have warned the first collapse may also have left the surrounding mountain slopes unstable, with concerns that further sections of ice or rock could break away, while cracks or fractures could develop in already weakened slopes, potentially triggering another landslide or flood.

"The slope seems like it was unstable and it is even unstable today because of this event," Tielidze said.

That uncertainty means authorities will be required to keep a close watch on the landscape, using helicopters, drones and satellite imagery alongside measurements of temperature, precipitation and river levels.

Tielidze said that while another flood on the same scale as the first is less likely, it cannot be ruled out.

The possibility of another flood is adding another layer of danger to an already difficult rescue operation.

The affected region is remote; roads and bridges have been destroyed, and communications have been disrupted.

"Helicopters are the main way to currently access some of those more difficult-to-reach areas," Australian Red Cross executive director of international programs Alex Mathieson said.

But Mathieson said limited helicopter capacity poses a "major challenge" which could force rescuers to prioritise where those resources are sent while accounting for the risk of further flooding.

He said the priority is to mobilise as many people and resources as possible, but local communities are also critical to the response.

"We know from experience that it's local people, it's local actors, that are absolutely most critical in response, particularly in those early days," Mathieson said.

The Nepal Red Cross has hundreds of staff and thousands of volunteers across the country, including people trained in first aid and disaster response.

"The big issue and big challenge is to get a really comprehensive assessment of the overall impact of the situation," Mathieson said.

body.zh: 灾难性山洪席卷尼泊尔和西藏边境沿线社区，造成尼泊尔和西藏至少 472 人死亡，目前至少有 1,400 人失踪。 据报道，救援工作仍在继续，有 39 名澳大利亚人失踪。 专家警告说，危险尚未结束，尼泊尔仍有可能再次发生灾难，尽管很难预测灾难发生的时间、地点和严重程度。 莫纳什大学冰川研究员莱万·蒂利泽（Levan Tielidze）表示：“这可能是第二天、几天后，也可能是几个月后，但再次发生如此规模的洪水的可能性较小。” 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 科学家警告说，第一次崩塌也可能导致周围山坡不稳定，人们担心更多的冰或岩石可能会脱落，而已经脆弱的山坡可能会出现裂缝或断裂，从而可能引发另一场山体滑坡或洪水。 “由于这次事件，斜坡似乎不稳定，今天甚至不稳定，”蒂利泽说。 这种不确定性意味着当局将需要使用直升机、无人机和卫星图像以及温度、降水和河流水位的测量来密切监视景观。 蒂利泽表示，虽然再次发生与第一次规模相同的洪水的可能性较小，但不能排除这种可能性。 再次发生洪水的可能性给本已困难的救援行动增添了另一层危险。 受影响地区地处偏远；道路和桥梁被毁，通讯中断。 澳大利亚红十字会国际项目执行主任亚历克斯·马蒂森表示：“直升机是目前进入一些较难到达地区的主要方式。” 但马蒂森表示，有限的直升机能力构成了“重大挑战”，这可能迫使救援人员优先考虑将这些资源发送到哪里，同时考虑到进一步洪水的风险。 他说，首要任务是动员尽可能多的人员和资源，但当地社区对应对措施也至关重要。 马蒂森说：“我们从经验中知道，当地人、当地演员在应对措施中绝对是最关键的，尤其是在早期。” 尼泊尔红十字会在全国拥有数百名工作人员和数千名志愿者，其中包括接受过急救和救灾培训的人员。 马蒂森说：“最大的问题和挑战是对局势的总体影响进行真正全面的评估。” 确定损失的全面规模需要时间，而基础设施仍然受损，而且……的威胁仍然存在。

reflection.en: As families rush toward the devastation in Nepal, the scale of the 538 confirmed deaths and 1,500 missing weighs heavily on the heart. When the mountains shake and the waters roar, we pray for the presence of Yahweh to be a tangible refuge for the grieving and a source of strength for the searchers. May those waiting for news find a peace that surpasses the...
reflection.zh: 随着家属们赶往尼泊尔的受灾现场，538名遇难者和1500名失踪者的惨剧沉重地压在人们心头。当山摇动、水咆哮之时，我们祈求雅伟的同在能成为哀恸者切实的避难所，并成为搜救人员的力量源泉。愿那些在焦灼中等待消息的人，能在那超越风暴混乱的平安中得着慰藉。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: At least 93,000 ‘in great need’ after Nepal-Tibet flash floods, says Red Cross
title.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏洪灾至少93,000人“急需援助”，红十字会称

summary.en: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) reports that at least 93,000 people may have been affected by flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border. The floods have resulted in over 540 deaths, 1,900 missing persons, and a large-scale rescue operation that is being hindered by the threat...
summary.zh: 国际红十字会与红新月会联合会（IFRC）报告称，尼泊尔-西藏边境的洪灾可能已影响到至少93,000人。此次洪灾已造成超过540人死亡，1,900人失踪，并引发了大规模的救援行动，但新的洪水威胁阻碍了救援工作。IFRC预计，随着救援人员进入偏远地区，死亡人数将继续上升。

body.en: Federation says it fears death toll of more than 540 will continue to rise as rescuers reach cut-off areas Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? The Red Cross has said at least 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday’s flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have killed more than 540 people, left another 1,900 missing, and triggered a huge rescue operation that is being hampered by fears of new flooding. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the world’s largest humanitarian network, said it feared the death toll would continue to rise as some of the hardest-hit areas remained inaccessible after roads and bridges were destroyed by the torrents. Continue reading...
body.zh: 联合会表示，随着救援人员到达隔离地区，担心死亡人数将继续上升，超过 540 人 尼泊尔-西藏山洪 - 最新更新 视觉指南：致命的洪水是如何展开的 告诉我们：您受到山洪的影响吗？红十字会表示，至少有 93,000 人可能受到周三尼泊尔-西藏边境山洪的影响，这场洪水已造成 540 多人死亡，另有 1,900 人失踪，并引发了一场大规模的救援行动，但由于担心会出现新的洪水，目前该行动受到阻碍。世界上最大的人道主义网络红十字会与红新月会国际联合会（IFRC）表示，由于道路和桥梁被洪流冲毁，一些受灾最严重的地区仍然无法进入，因此担心死亡人数将继续上升。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The devastating flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have left tens of thousands in 'great need.' In times of such widespread suffering, the call to compassion echoes loudly. Jesus taught that whatever we do for the least of these, we do for Him, reminding us of our profound connection to those in crisis.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境毁灭性的山洪暴发，使数万人陷入“急需援助”的困境。在如此广泛的苦难面前，怜悯的呼召响亮而清晰。耶稣教导我们，凡是为“最小的弟兄”做的，就是为祂做的，这提醒我们与处于危机中的人们有着深刻的联系。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 关于造成数百人死亡的尼泊尔-西藏洪水的已知信息

summary.en: Hundreds have died or are missing in Wednesday's flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 周三，尼泊尔和西藏边境发生洪水和山体滑坡，造成数百人死亡或失踪。

body.en:
Devastating landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.

At least 547 people have been killed and 977 people remain unaccounted for two days after floodwaters tore through the border region, sweeping away homes and roads, local officials have said.

Rescue workers say they now face a critical moment to reach remaining survivors as fears mount of further flooding in the disaster's aftermath.

Initial reports of an earthquake on the Nepal-Tibet border led many to believe that a tremor had caused a landslide, which in turn caused the devastating floods early on Wednesday.

However, the US Geological Survey (USGS) later confirmed that the disaster was caused by a "glacial collapse" - when a glacier or part of a glacier disintegrates.

The impact of the collapsed glacier hitting the bottom of a valley was so powerful that it registered a magnitude of 5.2, according to the agency, causing "subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream".

Powerful floodwaters and debris travelled some 62 miles (100km) downstream from the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi Rivers, the USGS said, sweeping through towns popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims in northern Nepal.

Footage showed a wall of mud and rock sweeping away buildings, roads and vehicles as people fled in the Nuwakot region.

In one video, a towering wall of water and mud was seen rushing down a gorge along the Trishuli River and enveloping the Rasuwagadhi Border checkpoint, a multi-storey building on the Nepalese side.

Gyirong Port, over the border, was also hit. A number of deaths were reported in Tibetan villages.

Scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events as rescue efforts continue. Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

"I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, [which] dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood," he told the BBC.

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIDMOD) has warned secondary flooding could occur in the coming days as a result of debris that washed into the river systems.

The ICIDMOD said it was assessing whether the Trishuli River had been temporarily blocked in narrow sections. If this is the case, it is at risk of forming a landslide dam and a second flood.

Separately, China has warned there was a "high risk" a lake that formed after the landslide may burst its banks, causing fresh flooding downstream. As of Friday, an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of water had accumulated, according to broadcaster CCTV.

State media reported that rescue operations were briefly...
body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生的毁灭性山体滑坡和山洪造成大面积破坏，造成数百人死亡或失踪。 当地官员表示，洪水席卷边境地区，冲毁房屋和道路，两天以来，至少有 547 人死亡，977 人下落不明。 救援人员表示，他们现在面临着救助剩余幸存者的关键时刻，因为人们越来越担心灾难发生后会发生进一步的洪水。 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生地震的初步报道让许多人相信地震导致了山体滑坡，进而导致了周三早些时候的毁灭性洪水。 然而，美国地质调查局（USGS）后来证实，这场灾难是由“冰川崩塌”造成的，即冰川或冰川的一部分崩解。 据该机构称，崩塌的冰川撞击山谷底部的冲击力非常强大，达到了 5.2 级，“随后对下游造成了灾难性影响”。 美国地质勘探局表示，强大的洪水和碎片从特里苏里河和博特科希河下游流过约 62 英里（100 公里），席卷了尼泊尔北部深受登山游客和朝圣者欢迎的城镇。 视频显示，努瓦科特地区的人们纷纷逃离，泥石墙冲走了建筑物、道路和车辆。 在一段视频中，人们看到一堵高耸的水和泥墙沿着特里苏里河冲下峡谷，包围了拉苏瓦加迪边境检查站，这是尼泊尔一侧的一座多层建筑。 边境另一边的吉隆口岸也受到袭击。据报道，西藏村庄已有多人死亡。 随着救援工作的继续，科学家们正试图拼凑出事件的确切顺序。牛津大学地球科学教授迈克·塞尔表示，在洪水袭击尼泊尔和西藏之前“几小时或几天”，冰川可能已经崩塌。 他告诉英国广播公司：“我认为，巨大的碎片浪潮表明，首先发生了山体滑坡，水堆积起来，堵塞了河流，然后引发了一场巨大的洪水。” 国际山地综合开发中心（ICIDMOD）警告称，由于碎片冲入河流系统，未来几天可能会发生二次洪水。 ICIDMOD 表示正在评估 Trishuli 河的狭窄河段是否被暂时堵塞。如果真是这样，就有形成滑坡坝和二次洪水的危险。 另外，中国警告说，山体滑坡后形成的湖泊存在“高风险”，可能会决堤，导致下游出现新的洪水。据中央电视台报道，截至周五，估计已积水 250 万立方米。 官方媒体报道称，救援行动短暂...

reflection.en: The earth groans, Scripture tells us, in a kind of shared labor pain until now (Romans 8:22). This week's devastating floods and landslides on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have claimed hundreds of lives and left many more missing, are a stark reminder of that groaning. In the face of such immense loss, we are called to lament with those who grieve and to...
reflection.zh: 圣经告诉我们，直到如今，全创造一直藉着生产之苦同声唉哼（罗马书 8:22）。本周在尼泊尔-西藏边境发生的毁灭性洪水和山体滑坡，已夺走了数百人的生命，另有许多人失踪，这是对那呻吟的严峻提醒。面对如此巨大的损失，我们被呼召与哀恸者一同哀哭，并祈求全创造的更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Nepal-Tibet flood death toll passes 500 as rescue resumes
title.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏洪灾死亡人数超过500人，救援工作恢复

summary.en: The Red Cross reports that over 93,000 people have been affected by deadly floods and landslides along the China-Nepal border. Rescue operations were temporarily halted due to an overflowing lake that threatened further flooding.
summary.zh: 红十字会报告称，中国-尼泊尔边境的致命洪水和山体滑坡已影响到超过93,000人。由于一个泛滥的湖泊威胁到进一步的洪水，救援行动曾一度暂停。

body.en:
The Red Cross says more than 93,000 people are affected by the deadly floods and landslides on the China-Nepal border. Rescue efforts were temporarily paused after an overflowing lake threatened to trigger more floods.

Rescue workers have resumed a search for hundreds of people still missing two days after  catastrophic flash flooding  hit the border between  Nepal and  China . 

Their efforts were briefly put on hold on Friday after a lake formed by debris began overflowing, threatening areas already devastated by the disaster.  

"We have received a notice saying that the lake has broken its banks," Narendra Pariyar, the most senior bureaucrat of the hard-hit Rasuwa district, told DW. "We can see that the level of water in the river is rising."

Residents in Nepal's border district of Rasuwa were seen fleeing up hillsides as they braced for a surge in river levels, Reuters reported.

Authorities later said the threat had eased but that they were closely monitoring the situation. 

Meanwhile, Nepal said the death toll had risen to 579,  up from 390 a day earlier . China has updated its earlier count of three to five deaths in Tibet.

More than 1,400 are still believed to be missing, including as many as 517 foreigners from more than 30 countries.

The International Red Cross estimated that over 93,000 people have been directly affected by the catastrophe and are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.

"We're of course very concerned about a secondary flood," said spokesman David Fisher at a press briefing in Geneva, adding that Red Cross relief trucks had been blocked by the lake which formed following the landslide.

Kamal Kishore, Head of the United ​Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, warned of further "cascading hazards that might unfold" and said: "The disaster is ⁠not ​yet completely over. It is still ​unfolding in some ways."

The World Health Organization (WHO) warned of the risk of disease in the wake of the disaster.

"Following a disaster of this scale, displacement, overcrowding ⁠and disruption ​to water, sanitation and health services can increase the risk of infectious diseases, including diarrhoea and respiratory illnesses," said spokesman Tarik ​Jasarevic.

Wednesday's disaster, triggered by a glacial collapse that sent rock and meltwater surging into rivers below, left a new danger in its wake: a barrier lake formed upstream by debris dams. 

China's Ministry of Water Resources said the lake held roughly 2 million cubic meters of water as of Thursday and was expected to receive another 3 million cubic meters — equivalent to about 1,200 Olympic swimming pools — over the following three days, with peak flow expected around...
body.zh: 红十字会表示，超过 93,000 人受到中尼边境致命洪水和山体滑坡的影响。由于湖水泛滥，可能引发更多洪水，救援工作暂时停止。 尼泊尔和中国边境发生灾难性山洪暴发两天后，救援人员已重新开始搜寻仍失踪的数百人。 周五，由于碎片形成的湖泊开始泛滥，威胁到已经遭受灾难破坏的地区，他们的努力被短暂搁置。 受灾最严重的拉苏瓦地区最高官员纳伦德拉·帕里亚尔 (Narendra Pariyar) 告诉德国之声：“我们收到通知，称该湖已决堤。” “我们可以看到河里的水位正在上升。” 据路透社报道，尼泊尔边境拉苏瓦地区的居民纷纷逃上山坡，以应对河流水位上涨的情况。 当局后来表示，威胁已经缓解，但他们正在密切关注事态发展。 与此同时，尼泊尔表示死亡人数已从一天前的 390 人上升至 579 人。 中国更新了此前西藏三至五人死亡的统计数据。 据信仍有 1,400 多人失踪，其中包括来自 30 多个国家的多达 517 名外国人。 国际红十字会估计，超过93,000人直接受到这场灾难的影响，急需人道援助。 发言人大卫·费舍尔在日内瓦举行的新闻发布会上表示：“我们当然非常担心二次洪水。”他补充说，红十字会的救援卡车被山体滑坡后形成的湖泊堵塞。 联合国减少灾害风险办公室主任卡迈勒·基肖尔警告称，“可能会出现更多连锁危险”，并表示：“灾难尚未完全结束。在某些方面，它仍在继续发展。” 世界卫生组织（WHO）就灾难发生后的疾病风险发出警告。 发言人塔里克·贾萨雷维奇 (Tarik Jasarevic) 表示：“如此规模的灾难发生后，流离失所、过度拥挤以及供水、卫生和医疗服务中断可能会增加感染腹泻和呼吸道疾病等传染病的风险。” 周三的灾难是由冰川崩塌引发的，冰川崩塌导致岩石和融水涌入下面的河流，随之而来的是一个新的危险：上游由碎片坝形成的堰塞湖。 中国水利部表示，截至周四，该湖的蓄水量约为 200 万立方米，预计在接下来的三天内将再接收 300 万立方米的水，相当于约 1,200 个奥运会游泳池的水量，预计高峰流量将在...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans, bearing the weight of a fallen world, as seen in the devastating floods and landslides along the China-Nepal border. In the midst of such natural fury, we pray for those affected, for the rescuers working tirelessly, and for the eventual renewal of all creation.
reflection.zh: 大地本身也在哀鸣，承受着堕落世界的重负，正如中国-尼泊尔边境毁灭性的洪水和山体滑坡所显示的。在这自然的愤怒中，我们为受影响的人们、为不知疲倦的救援人员祈祷，并为万物终将得到更新而祈求。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Watch: Why rescuers fear new barrier lake could cause another Nepal-Tibet flood
title.zh: 视频：为何救援人员担心新的堰塞湖可能引发另一次尼泊尔-西藏洪水

summary.en: Laura Bicker explains how a lake that formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border is raising fears of a second flood.
summary.zh: 劳拉·比克解释了尼泊尔-西藏边境附近最近一次山体滑坡后形成的一个湖泊如何引发了对第二次洪水的担忧。

body.en:
China has warned there is a "high risk" that a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.

The warning comes after Wednesday's deadly flash flood in the same area which scientists say was triggered by the collapse of a mountain glacier into a river.
body.zh: 中国警告称，最近尼泊尔和西藏边境附近发生山体滑坡后形成的湖泊存在“高风险”，可能会冲破河岸，导致下游发生第二次洪水。 这一警告是在周三同一地区发生致命的山洪之后发出的，科学家称这场洪水是由山地冰川崩塌入河引发的。

reflection.en: The earth groans, a creation groaning in labor pains, as the Bible says. The recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border has created a barrier lake, raising fears of another devastating flood. This natural disaster reminds us of the fragility of our world and the deep impact of decay on all of creation.
reflection.zh: 正如圣经所说，大地在呻吟，受造之物如同在产难之中一同呻吟。尼泊尔-西藏边境附近最近发生的一次山体滑坡形成了一个堰塞湖，引发了对另一次毁灭性洪水的担忧。这场自然灾害提醒我们世界的脆弱性，以及衰败对整个受造之物造成的深远影响。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: This Indian pilgrim was about to enter Tibet for her dream tour - then her WhatsApp messages stopped
title.zh: 这位印度朝圣者即将进入西藏进行她梦想中的旅行——然后她的WhatsApp消息停止了

summary.en: Her family is among hundreds anxiously waiting for news after the deadly flash floods.
summary.zh: 在致命的洪水之后，她的家人是数百个焦急等待消息的人之一。

body.en:
Early on Wednesday, Sudipto Bhattacharya received what would be the last messages from his wife.

She'd sent a picture of a departure stamp in her passport at 07:57 (02:27 GMT) - immigration at the Nepal border was done.

Six minutes later, at 08:03, she wrote: we are waiting to enter China. Then the messages stopped.

Subhrasree Chakraborty and the group she was travelling with had been waiting to cross into Tibet for the next stage of their pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, the sacred Himalayan home of Hindu god Shiva that Subhrasree had dreamed of visiting for years.

The 43-year-old is now among at least 290 Indians reported missing after deadly flash floods struck along Nepal's border with Tibet. Many of those unaccounted for were on the pilgrimage, which resumed last year after being disrupted by the pandemic and then by tensions between India and China. Thousands of Indians have been making their way to Mount Kailash for years.

Subhrasree was travelling without her family, as part of a group of about 30 people. A medical technologist working in critical care at a city hospital, she was used to emergencies. She knew CPR and intensive-care procedures and, according to her husband, was physically fit.

But none of that has brought her husband Sudipto Bhattacharya any closer to knowing what happened after that final message.

The photographs she sent home from Kathmandu, taken just days before she went missing, capture something of that excitement.

In one, she stands in a blue tunic in the ornate courtyard of a temple, smiling gently at the camera. In others, she is dressed in red, posing by the ancient brick-and-carved-wood architecture of Kathmandu valley's historic Durbar Square.

"She was very excited," says Bhattacharya, a government officer. "This was her dream tour."

She took the Mithila Express from Kolkata and reached Raxaul on 22 August. From there she crossed into Birgunj and travelled by bus to Kathmandu, arriving that night.

Then, on the morning of 25 August, the group left Kathmandu by bus for Syabrubesi, a small mountain settlement roughly 122km north of Kathmandu and a gateway to the trekking hub of Langtang region. The journey took almost 12 hours - and was not entirely a smooth one.

A landslide blocked their route for about four hours before the army cleared the road. But when Subhrasree spoke to her husband, she told him the skies were clear.

"She kept saying the weather was good," he says. "She said it was rather warm, it was raining sometimes."

Bhattacharya spoke to her on the phone, and the two continued messaging afterwards. Around an hour later, she told him the Nepal immigration formalities were complete and that the group was waiting to cross into Tibet.

body.zh: 周三早些时候，苏迪普托·巴塔查亚收到了妻子发来的最后一条信息。 她于 07:57（格林威治标准时间 02:27）发送了一张护照上盖有离境印章的照片 - 尼泊尔边境的入境手续已经完成。 六分钟后，08:03，她写道：我们正在等待进入中国。然后消息就停止了。 Subhrasree Chakraborty 和与她同行的团队一直在等待进入西藏，前往冈仁波齐峰朝圣，这是 Subhrasree 多年来一直梦想参观的印度教湿婆神喜马拉雅山的神圣家园。 尼泊尔与西藏边境发生致命的山洪爆发后，据报道至少有 290 名印度人失踪，这名 43 岁的男子是其中之一。许多下落不明的人都在参加朝圣活动，该朝圣活动因疫情和印度与中国之间的紧张局势而中断，并于去年恢复。多年来，成千上万的印度人一直前往冈仁波齐峰。 Subhrasree 和大约 30 人一起旅行，没有家人陪伴。她是一名在市立医院重症监护室工作的医疗技术专家，已经习惯了紧急情况。据她丈夫说，她了解心肺复苏术和重症监护程序，而且身体健康。 但所有这些都没有让她的丈夫苏迪普托·巴塔查亚 (Sudipto Bhattacharya) 更加了解在最后一条信息之后发生了什么。 她从加德满都寄回家的照片是在她失踪前几天拍摄的，捕捉到了那种兴奋的感觉。 在其中一张照片中，她穿着蓝色外衣站在一座寺庙华丽的庭院里，对着镜头温柔地微笑。在其他照片中，她身着红衣，在加德满都谷地历史悠久的杜巴广场的古老砖雕木建筑前摆姿势。 “她非常兴奋，”政府官员巴塔查里亚 (Bhattacharya) 说。 “这是她梦想的巡演。” 她从加尔各答乘坐 Mithila Express 并于 8 月 22 日到达拉克索尔。她从那里进入比尔甘杰，然后乘坐巴士前往加德满都，并于当晚抵达。 然后，8 月 25 日早上，一行人乘坐巴士离开加德满都，前往 Syabrubesi，这是加德满都以北约 122 公里处的一个小山区定居点，也是通往 Langtang 地区徒步中心的门户。这段旅程花费了近 12 个小时，而且并不完全顺利。 山体滑坡封锁了他们的路线约四个小时，之后军队才清理道路。但当苏布拉斯里与她的丈夫交谈时，她告诉他天空晴朗。 “她一直说天气很好，”他说。 “她说天气很热，有时会下雨。” 巴塔查亚通过电话与她交谈，随后两人继续发消息。大约一个小时后，她告诉他尼泊尔入境手续已经完成，一行人正在等待进入西藏。 在办理完尼泊尔出入境手续后，朝圣者穿过边境...

Her last messages to her family abruptly stopped, leaving them in anxious uncertainty. title.en: How Australians can help those impacted by devastating Nepal floods
title.zh: 澳大利亚人如何帮助受尼泊尔毁灭性洪水影响的人们

summary.en: Australian charities have launched a joint appeal to aid communities devastated by floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border. Thousands are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean water, and medical care after their homes and infrastructure were destroyed.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚慈善机构已发起联合募捐，以援助尼泊尔-中国边境受洪水和山体滑坡摧毁的社区。在房屋和基础设施被毁后，成千上万的人迫切需要住所、食物、清洁饮用水和医疗援助。

body.en:
Entire communities have been devastated by severe flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border, with homes, roads, bridges and critical infrastructure destroyed.

Search and rescue operations remain underway, while thousands of people are in urgent need of shelter, food, clean drinking water and medical assistance.

In response, 14 Australian charities have joined forces to launch a national appeal.

The Emergency Action Alliance (EAA) has launched the Nepal Flood Disaster Appeal, bringing together a variety of charities to support communities affected by the disaster.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The alliance says donations will help provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water, hygiene supplies and medical care.

Access to some affected communities remains difficult, with damaged roads and ongoing weather conditions hampering efforts to reach people in need.

Australians are encouraged to donate through the EAA website or by calling 1300 939 000.

The charities participating in the appeal are Save the Children Australia, Plan International Australia, Oxfam Australia, Australia for UNHCR, ActionAid Australia, CARE Australia, Caritas Australia, ADRA, Act for Peace, Anglican Overseas Aid, Australian Lutheran World Service, Baptist World Aid Australia, CBM Australia and Tearfund Australia.

EAA executive director Kerren Morris said the appeal provided Australians with a trusted way to support people affected by the disaster.

"Emergency shelter, food, safe drinking water and medical support are urgently needed now, while longer-term recovery efforts will continue for many months," she said in a statement.

The charities involved bring different areas of humanitarian expertise to the response, with organisations and their local partners working to provide immediate assistance to affected communities.

Save the Children is focusing on supporting children and families affected by humanitarian emergencies.

Oxfam Australia's humanitarian work includes support for essential services such as clean water, sanitation and emergency assistance.

Australia for UNHCR is the UN refugee agency's national partner in Australia, and is supporting humanitarian assistance through the UNHCR network.

The charities involved are continuing to assess the scale of the disaster and humanitarian needs in affected communities.

The EAA says its members are working to determine where support is most urgently needed as search and rescue operations continue.

The appeal has been endorsed by the Australian Council for International Development (ACFID), the peak body for Australian non-government organisations...
body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境沿线的严重洪水和山体滑坡摧毁了整个社区，房屋、道路、桥梁和重要基础设施被毁。 搜救行动仍在进行中，数千人迫切需要住所、食物、清洁饮用水和医疗援助。 作为回应，14家澳大利亚慈善机构联手发起全国呼吁。 紧急行动联盟（EAA）发起了尼泊尔洪灾呼吁，汇集了各种慈善机构来支持受灾社区。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 该联盟表示，捐款将有助于提供紧急人道主义援助，包括紧急住所、食品、安全饮用水、卫生用品和医疗服务。 进入一些受影响的社区仍然很困难，道路受损和持续的天气状况阻碍了援助有需要的人的努力。 我们鼓励澳大利亚人通过 EAA 网站或致电 1300 939 000 进行捐款。 参与呼吁的慈善机构包括澳大利亚救助儿童会、澳大利亚国际计划、澳大利亚乐施会、澳大利亚难民署、澳大利亚行动援助组织、澳大利亚援外社、澳大利亚明爱、ADRA、和平行动、圣公会海外援助、澳大利亚路德会世界服务社、澳大利亚浸信会世界援助组织、澳大利亚 CBM 和澳大利亚泪基金。 EAA 执行董事 Kerren Morris 表示，这一呼吁为澳大利亚人提供了一种值得信赖的方式来支持受灾难影响的人们。 她在一份声明中说：“现在迫切需要紧急住所、食物、安全饮用水和医疗支持，而长期恢复工作将持续数月。” 参与其中的慈善机构将不同领域的人道主义专业知识融入到应对工作中，组织及其当地合作伙伴致力于为受影响的社区提供即时援助。 救助儿童会的重点是支持受人道主义紧急情况影响的儿童和家庭。 澳大利亚乐施会的人道主义工作包括支持清洁水、卫生设施和紧急援助等基本服务。 联合国难民署澳大利亚办事处是联合国难民署在澳大利亚的国家合作伙伴，并通过难民署网络支持人道主义援助。 相关慈善机构正在继续评估灾难的规模和受影响社区的人道主义需求。 EAA 表示，随着搜救行动的继续，其成员正在努力确定哪里最需要支持。 该呼吁得到了澳大利亚非政府组织最高机构澳大利亚国际发展委员会（ACFID）的认可......

reflection.en: The devastating floods in Nepal have left entire communities in urgent need of basic necessities. This situation calls us to action, reminding us of our responsibility to advocate for the vulnerable and provide tangible support to those facing such immense hardship. Proverbs 31:8-9 urges us to 'Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔毁灭性的洪水使整个社区迫切需要基本生活必需品。这种情况呼唤我们采取行动，提醒我们有责任为弱势群体发声，并为那些面临巨大困难的人提供切实的支持。《箴言》31:8-9 敦促我们：“你们要为不能说话的辩护，为所有孤苦者伸张正义。你们要开口说话，公正地审判，为困苦和贫穷的人伸张正义。”

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.

title.en: Nepal floods: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪灾：数百人死亡，一千多人失踪

summary.en: Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.
summary.zh: 救援队正在搜寻幸存者，此前一次冰川崩塌引发了尼泊尔和西藏的灾难性洪水。包括许多外国游客在内的数百人失踪。

body.en:
Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.

The death toll from catastrophic flash floods along the border between  Nepal  and Tibet has risen to at least 392, while more than 1,400 people were missing.

Rescue teams were searching for survivors on Thursday, a day after a glacial collapse sent a huge wall of mud and rock barreling through the Himalayan communities, sweeping away entire villages.

Even with rescue efforts underway, local authorities warned that a fresh disaster could occur as a lake that had formed due to the floodwaters was threatening to burst.

In Tibet, Chinese broadcaster CCTV reported 558 people missing in Gyirong county, including 260 foreigners. Three deaths had been confirmed there as of Thursday morning, with two villagers rescued.

The disaster struck Wednesday when a glacial collapse triggered a flood in the Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, in a corridor popular with trekkers and pilgrims connecting Kathmandu with Lhasa. 

Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters the death toll "will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered."

Neighboring India accounts for the largest proportion of missing foreign nationals. Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said that 288 Indians were unaccounted for in Nepal, while a further 200 were stranded in China awaiting rescue.

US officials said around 90 US citizens remained unaccounted for on Thursday. The US State Department said three have been rescued, but that it was not yet aware of any deaths among US citizens.

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal tourism board spokesperson, told the AP news agency that many of the missing were pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus. In addition to the Indian and US tourists, Sharma said 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians were also missing.

Reuters cited other police and tourism officials who put the missing tourists at 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.

China's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were unaccounted for. 

During a press conference in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said they were still verifying the breakdown of nationalities of the missing foreigners in Tibet, who were mostly tourists and pilgrims.

China authorities said they were in close communication ‌with Nepal on search and rescue efforts.

Chinese premier Li Qiang has traveled to affected areas in Tibet to view the emergency work, state media reported.

body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏冰川崩塌引发灾难性洪水后，救援队正在寻找幸存者。数百人失踪，其中包括许多外国游客。 尼泊尔和西藏边境的特大山洪造成的死亡人数已上升至至少 392 人，另有 1,400 多人失踪。 周四，救援队正在寻找幸存者，一天前，冰川崩塌导致一面巨大的泥土和岩石墙穿过喜马拉雅社区，席卷了整个村庄。 尽管救援工作正在进行，但地方当局警告称，由于洪水形成的湖泊有决堤的危险，可能会发生新的灾难。 在西藏，中国中央电视台报道吉隆县有 558 人失踪，其中包括 260 名外国人。截至周四上午，该地区已确认三人死亡，两名村民获救。 灾难于周三发生，冰川崩塌引发博特科希河支流伦德科拉河洪水泛滥，该河是连接加德满都和拉萨的徒步旅行者和朝圣者常去的走廊。 尼泊尔警方发言人阿比·纳拉扬·卡夫勒 (Abi Narayan Kafle) 告诉路透社，死亡人数“将会上升，因为我们已经恢复搜索，预计将找到更多尸体。” 邻国印度在失踪外国人中所占比例最大。印度外交部长苏杰生表示，有 288 名印度人在尼泊尔下落不明，另有 200 人滞留在中国等待救援。 美国官员表示，周四仍有约 90 名美国公民下落不明。美国国务院表示，三人已获救，但尚不清楚有美国公民死亡。 尼泊尔旅游局发言人苏尼尔·夏尔马 (Sunil Sharma) 告诉美联社，许多失踪者是前往西藏冈仁波齐峰的朝圣者，冈仁波齐峰是印度教徒的圣地。夏尔马说，除了印度和美国游客外，还有 34 名澳大利亚人、33 名英国人和 24 名加拿大人失踪。 路透社援引其他警方和旅游官员的话说，失踪的游客中有 34 名来自澳大利亚，33 名来自英国，25 名来自加拿大。 与此同时，中国外交部表示，近100名中国公民下落不明。 外交部发言人林健在北京举行的新闻发布会上表示，他们仍在核实西藏失踪外国人的国籍，这些人主要是游客和朝圣者。 中国当局表示，他们正在与尼泊尔就搜救工作保持密切沟通。 据官方媒体报道，中国总理李强已前往西藏受灾地区查看应急工作。 随着灾难的规模变得...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans under the weight of sin and disaster, as this devastating flood in Nepal and Tibet illustrates. In the midst of such overwhelming loss, we remember that creation itself awaits redemption, and we pray for comfort for those affected and for the eventual renewal of all things.
reflection.zh: 大地本身在罪恶和灾难的重压下呻吟，尼泊尔和西藏这场毁灭性的洪水便是明证。在如此巨大的损失面前，我们当铭记受造之物本身都在等待救赎，并祈求受灾者得到安慰，以及万物终将得到更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal floods climbs to 35
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
The Nepal Tourism Board says 35 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 273 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

That number had been 34 until the tourism board published an update Thursday afternoon.

Another 823 people, including 644 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

On Thursday afternoon, China's foreign minister said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were missing, revising down earlier reporting in Chinese state media that 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were missing in Gyirong Port, Tibet.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

A US-based tour company Himalayan Glacier Adventures told ABC News that 15 Australians, part of a group of 47 people, were on a hiking tour in the Lantang Valley at the time of the landslides.

The group of Australians was comprised of nine men and six women. Two of those Australians were reportedly boys aged 11 and 14, and a woman aged 64.

Tilak Pokharel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre, said there were "a lot" of people in Melbourne waiting anxiously to hear from loved ones.

"There are a lot of people affected by the flood. There are many people from that area living in Melbourne," Pokharel said.

body.zh: 周三，尼泊尔和西藏边境发生大规模洪水和山体滑坡灾害，造成至少 160 人死亡，数百人失踪，其中据报道有 34 名澳大利亚人。 援助人员表示，整个定居点已被“摧毁”。法新社证实的监控录像显示，一股故事高的碎片撞向边境地区的中国一侧，将卡车和公共汽车抛到一边，数十人逃命。 中国官方媒体报道称，西藏边境枢纽发生泥石流，造成“重大人员伤亡”，其中三人死亡，另有 265 人失踪。 尼泊尔警方表示，他们在“毁灭性洪水”后已找到 157 具尸体，官员“正在努力将洪水风险地区的家庭转移到更安全的地方”。 洪水淹没了多层建筑的较低楼层后，救援人员在泥浆中涉水寻找幸存者。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 据尼泊尔旅游部称，灾难发生后数小时内，约 403 名游客（其中 341 名外国人）下落不明。 旅游局发言人向美国广播公司新闻提供的一份名单显示，失踪的澳大利亚人人数为 34 人。 外交贸易部 (DFAT) 尚未确认该数字。 外交贸易部发言人告诉 SBS 新闻：“我们知道该地区有许多澳大利亚人，澳大利亚官员正在紧急努力确认他们的福利。” “我们正在与地方当局以及旅行社联络。” 旅游局称，失踪的外国人包括 142 名印度人，以及来自澳大利亚、英国、马来西亚、荷兰、葡萄牙、南非、韩国和美国的其他人。 红十字会与红新月会国际联合会（IFRC）尼泊尔负责人戴维·费舍尔（David Fisher）表示：“整个村庄和市场区域都被夷为平地。” 该公司表示正在发送紧急物资，包括毯子、急救箱、担架和裹尸袋。 他在社交媒体上发表声明说：“你们所遭受的痛苦和损失并不小。” “但我想向你们保证，在这个困难时期，你们并不孤单——国家将竭尽全力与你们同在。” 当地人受到了创伤，而专家警告说，河流的持续堵塞可能会引发额外的洪水。 “今天早上我接到（我姐夫）的电话，他们哭着说他们的整个房子都被冲走了。三名家庭成员获救，但他的兄弟仍然失踪，”当地56岁的拉朱·巴德尔说。 但尼泊尔外交部长希希尔·卡纳尔表示，地震可能引发山体滑坡，从而阻碍了...

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪、整个定居点“被夷为平地”的消息，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此大规模的毁灭和生命损失面前，“雅伟哭了”这简短的经文提醒我们，悲伤是一种自然而神圣的回应。雅伟在基督里分担我们人类的痛苦，当言语无法表达时，祂提供了一个充满怜悯的同在。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。
